title: Reserve special forces personnel protest over unpaid state compensation
organizer: Reserve personnel of the Special Purpose Forces from Nakhchivan; formal organizer unknown
threshold_50_evidence: Source confirms a public protest but provides no number of people present. The 24 figure counts benefit recipients said to be unpaid, not attendees; threshold is unproven.

occurrence.summary: VOA says reserve servicemen protested on 8 October outside the Presidential Administration.

start_date.summary: Article states the protest occurred on 8 October 2024.

organizer.summary: Participants are identified as reserve special forces servicemen from Nakhchivan; organizer not named.

demands.summary: They demanded overdue one-time compensation equivalent to 36 months of salary.

participants.summary: No attendee count. Reported 24 is number of affected servicemen, not protest turnout.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Threshold unresolved: no simultaneous attendance estimate.

state_response.summary: Police reportedly did not intervene; the group later met at the Presidential Administration and was told an inquiry/meeting would follow.

protester_violence.summary: No description sufficient to code protester violence.

notes: This is an October action concerning state-administered benefits. The later 26 November gathering concerns the same unresolved matter; whether that later date is a new protest event or a repeated visit within one episode remains open. One source reports 24 unpaid beneficiaries, not 24 protesters. Demand-category fit as labor/wage dispute is provisional because the claim concerns a retirement benefit calculated from salary.
